subject: Post-call: PayGrid model fit & parity discussion / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <s.turner@paygrid.com>, Alex Morales <alex.morales@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: PayGrid model fit & parity discussion / next steps

Hi Sam / Alex —

Thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete next steps we agreed on: 

Summary of needs (as we heard them)
- Primary goal: replace PayGrid-Base for transaction categorization and automated explanations while matching or exceeding accuracy and reducing per-token cost.
- Acceptance criteria you mentioned: parity on intent/classification F1 (~within 2–3 points), factuality/hallucination rates below ~2–3%, and latency under 350ms p95 for typical requests.
- Data: you’ll share a representative prompt set + 500 labeled examples for parity checks.

Recommended initial model candidates (open / cost-conscious):
- Llama 2-Chat 70B (quantized) — good baseline for high-quality chat-like completions
- Mistral-Instruct (33B) — strong instruction-following at lower cost
- Redw-Open-1.3 (our tuned open checkpoint) — best cost-quality tradeoff in our benchmarks for structured outputs

What we will deliver next
1) Run a parity evaluation comparing the three candidate open models vs your PayGrid-Base on the prompt set you provide. We’ll measure intent F1, top-1 accuracy, hallucination/factuality proxy, latency distribution, and token cost.
2) Share a short eval report (PDF) + the prompt set with annotations and suggested prompt improvements.
3) Schedule a 60-min SE deep-dive to review failure cases and plan canary rollout if results look good.

Attachments: I attached the prompt set you gave during the call (paygrid_prompt_set_v1.csv).

Next steps (proposed timeline)
- You: confirm the final prompt set and drop the 500 labeled examples in the Drive folder (by EOD Thu 3/5)
- Us: run initial parity eval and share results within 7 business days of receiving the labeled set
- Schedule: Aditya, can you propose 2 windows for the SE deep-dive next week?

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123
From: Sam Turner <s.turner@paygrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayGrid model fit & parity discussion / next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Parity thresholds: the 2–3 point F1 window is what we were thinking. We’d also like to see a breakdown by category (refunds, chargebacks, transfers) since performance varies.
2) Hallucination: the <2% threshold is a hard requirement for the explanation generator. If any model shows >2% hallucination we can’t roll it to production without guardrails.
3) Baseline: we’ll provide a snapshot of PayGrid-Base (inference outputs + labels) for the labeled sample. Will that be sufficient for a fair comparison?

We can upload the 500 labeled examples and the PayGrid-Base snapshot to the Drive folder by EOD Thu 3/5.

We’re available for the SE deep-dive on Tue 3/9 after 11am ET or Wed 3/10 morning.

Also — any preliminary guidance on deployment modes? We expect to start on hosted, but may move to dedicated capacity if throughput grows.

Cheers,
Sam
Sr. ML Product Manager, PayGrid
s.turner@paygrid.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <s.turner@paygrid.com>, Alex Morales <alex.morales@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayGrid model fit & parity discussion / next steps

Hi Sam — thanks for the clarifying q’s. A few technical notes that should help set expectations for the parity run: 

Evaluation methodology (high level)- We’ll run each candidate model on your prompt set and compute: intent/classification F1 per category, top-1 output match rate vs PayGrid-Base, a simple hallucination proxy (named entity drift + unsupported numeric changes), token cost, and latency p50/p95 on a representative instance pool.

Deployment & config notes- Quantization: we’ll run 8-bit quantized variants where available to match cost targets and to measure any quality delta.
- Prompt engineering: small canonicalization (protected tokens, instruction headers) often reduces hallucination—we’ll include suggested prompt_set_v1 canonicalized examples in the report.

Acceptance thresholds (proposal)
- Intent/class F1: within -3 to +inf points of PayGrid-Base (i.e., no more than 3 points lower)
- Hallucination proxy: <= 2% (hard requirement for explanations)
- Latency: p95 < 350ms for typical single-turn requests (we’ll include batching/caching guidance if throughput requires)

Preliminary expected outcomes (based on our internal benchmarks)
- Llama 2-Chat 70B (8-bit): high precision, slightly higher latency/cost than Mistral; should be within parity on many categories but may need prompt tuning on numeric extraction.
- Mistral-Instruct (33B): excellent cost/throughput; may need more prompt engineering for edge categories.
- Redw-Open-1.3: best overall balance in our public benchmarks for structured outputs; often within 1–2 F1 points of many proprietary baselines.

Attachments: initial eval scaffold and an internal quick-report (paygrid_eval_report_initial.pdf) with example trade-offs.

If PayGrid can share the labeled set and the PayGrid-Base outputs, we’ll run the parity harness and aim to get a first-pass report back by Tue 3/10 (assuming we receive artifacts on Thu 3/5).

—
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: PayGrid model fit & parity discussion / next steps

Thanks team — appreciate the quick responses and alignment. Finalizing next steps & timeline here so it’s explicit: 

1) PayGrid action (by EOD Thu 3/5) — upload: (a) 500 labeled examples CSV, (b) PayGrid-Base outputs for those examples, (c) any category priority notes to the shared Drive folder.
2) Redwood action (target): run parity eval across the three candidate open models + our recommended config tweaks; deliver initial eval report by Tue 3/10.
3) SE deep-dive (60m): Tue 3/9 11:30am ET (we’ll send calendar invite) — agenda: review failure cases, discuss canary rollout metrics, and deployment options (hosted -> dedicated).

We’ll treat hallucination <=2% as a gating requirement for explanations; if none of the open models meet that requirement we’ll surface fallback options (hybrid approach with supervised scoring or a constrained generation layer).

I attached a short mutual action plan doc (paygrid_mutual_action_plan_20260304.docx) with milestones and owners.

If anything here looks off, flag it and we’ll correct. Otherwise I’ll send the invite for 3/9.

Thanks —
